title: Consolidate Redis + Kafka worker shims into single event-loop runtime to reduce duplicated buffering and improve backpressure
creator: Riley Patel
description:
Problem: Over the last two years we accrued parallel, divergent worker shims for Redis streams and Kafka consumers. Each shim implements its own buffering, retry orchestration, and backpressure heuristics. The duplication has led to subtle behavioral differences (e.g., how retry budgets interact with backoff windows) and makes cross-tenant behavior hard to reason about. We also observe duplicated in-memory buffers and extra goroutines per shard that increase GC pressure and tail latency under bursty load.

Goal: Replace the two ad-hoc shims with a single lightweight event-loop runtime that can host both Redis and Kafka adapters. The unified runtime should: 1) centralize buffering and backpressure policies, 2) provide a pluggable retry policy layer used by both adapters, 3) reduce per-shard goroutine count by at least 40%, and 4) preserve existing SLA behavior (no regression to p95/p99 latency under typical production traffic).

Scope: Implement event-loop runtime, translate existing Redis/Kafka adapters to use the runtime interface, migrate one non-critical tenant to validate runtime, add telemetry for buffer occupancy and retry counts, and update operator docs. This ticket focuses on the core runtime + two adapters; follow-up tickets will cover canary automation and Dedicated-capacity tuning.
acceptance_criteria: Single runtime binary hosting both adapters with runtime flag --event-loop-enabled
End-to-end integration test suite exercising retry/requeue/redelivery scenarios for both Redis and Kafka
Observed >=40% reduction in peak goroutine counts during synthetic burst test compared to baseline
Backpressure metrics (buffer_utilization, shed_count) are emitted and show correct throttling behavior under load
No regression in p95/p99 token latency for control workload in the staging environment
rollout_plan: Merge runtime + adapter PRs behind feature flag
Deploy to staging and run synthetic harness (redis-streams + kafka-shard) for 2h
Canary to single non-critical tenant for 48h with live traffic shadowing; monitor drop/shed/retry counts
Progressively enable for 10%, 30%, 100% of tenants with automated rollback if shed_count > threshold or consumer-lag spikes
Post-rollout: run 72h soak, then remove old shims from binary and perform cleanup
testing_plan: Unit tests for runtime event-loop invariants (drain, pause, resume)
Chaos tests: kill adapter goroutine and assert redis/kafka redelivery within SLA
Load tests: 5-minute burst, 1M messages/hour baseline, measure memory/goroutines
Regression suite: run existing e2e scenarios that previously exposed retry budget interactions
Integration with CI to run against a local redis/kafka fixture with deterministic timing
notes: Implementation will reuse the existing token-bucket code but move the policy decision into the runtime core
We need to coordinate with Observability team to add new metrics to the runtime metrics schema
Potential risk: some customers rely on subtle timing differences of old shims; keep retention of old behavior behind flag for 2 weeks
Follow-ups: canary automation ticket, Dedicated autoscaler tuning for runtime, doc updates for private deployment
